extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and journalists/editors evaluating press releases
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist of ethical and practical criteria for press releases aimed at maximizing news pickup: focuses on transparency, verifiability, public interest, and editorial cooperation derived from Ivy Lee's 1906 Declaration of Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness about source
rubrics_metrics.description: "This is not a secret press bureau. All our work is done in the open." Does the release disclose, on its face, who issued it and on whose behalf?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release should clearly state the originator and client; anti-patterns include anonymous communiqués or releases hidden behind pseudonymous channels. Openness is a core differentiator from press-agentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplying news, not advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: "We aim to supply news." Does the release contain genuine news rather than concealed promotional copy formatted to look like a news item?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should present factual, newsworthy information rather than promotional puffery. Editors should watch for disguised ads or copy that primarily markets rather than informs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our matter is accurate." Are the facts in the release verifiable and free of exaggeration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be factual and supportable; avoid hyperbole or unverifiable assertions. Accuracy affects credibility and likelihood of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-verification offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee offered help "to verify directly any statement of fact." Does the release make sources, raw data, or contact information available so an editor can independently check claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sources, data, and named contacts to enable independent verification. Failure to enable verification lowers editorial trust and pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named, identifiable issuer
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release name the principal (the corporation, candidate, agency) on whose behalf it is sent — never anonymous, never falsely sourced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always identify the principal clearly; ambiguous or misleading sourcing undermines editorial use and violates the Declaration's standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest test
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is offered only on subjects "of value and interest to the public to know about." Does the release pass a public-interest threshold, or is it of interest only to the issuer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the content has genuine public value beyond the issuer's promotional aims. Releases of purely self-interested material score poorly on pickup-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Details on any subject treated will be supplied promptly." Does the release indicate channels for follow-up (named spokesperson, phone, address) rather than dead-end attribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, prompt contact paths (spokesperson, phone, address) for follow-up information; vague or unreachable contacts reduce usability for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee committed to assisting editors "cheerfully" with additional information. Does the release support, rather than substitute for, independent reporting (e.g., supplemental backgrounders, image rights, expert availability)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer to assist editors with background, materials, or interviews; cooperative behavior (timely responses, providing assets) increases pickup and fosters relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: No suppression of unfavorable matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit in "in the open": does the release acknowledge, rather than conceal, material context that an editor would want?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid omitting relevant negative context or facts; transparency about unfavorable matters is part of ethical disclosure and preserves editorial trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee insisted releases be signed by an accountable individual, not issued anonymously. Is there a named, contactable PR officer of record?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases should be signed or clearly attributable to a responsible person who can be contacted; anonymous releases violate this principle and lower credibility.
